correctness.rationale: Exact capped impulse response and strict opposite monotonicity yield a unique all-location crossing for all \(0<a<b,\ L_0>0,\ \Delta>0\). Fully capped response gives sharp critical dose and plateau; un-clipped explicit postpeak gives lower-dose branch. Nondegenerate pristine sag curvature and an envelope expansion establish square-root small-dose law and next-order risk. Standard-library checker replay passed 48022 numerical diagnostics; general proof is analytic.

evidence: The present reset is D(s+)=max(D(s-)-Delta,0), equivalent to a location-dependent fractional reset only after fixing s. The closest fractional result assumes a constant residual fraction q at all sites.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A fixed dose induces \(q(s)=\max\{0,1-\Delta/g(s)\}\) depending on placement, so the constant \(q\) fractional theorem is not applicable globally. The generalized minimax condition of equalizing limiting peaks is acknowledged prior art; the explicit dosage frontier and its square-root singularity are separate claims.

value.rationale: Absolute fixed dose with a physical saturation cap is a mathematically distinct, motivated river-management control. The theorem gives a globally exhaustive dose-to-site/risk classification with a sharp dose plateau and leading square-root sensitivity near zero dose, quantitatively differentiating optimal placement from efficiency-based unassisted-sag positioning. The model is explicitly idealized and does not claim empirical effectiveness.
